answer: Agents stake a bonded deposit to join, and each epoch they must submit a unique proof-of-work challenge keyed to their identity plus a randomly assigned lagoon coordinate, making mass fake identities expensive to seed and maintain. A reputation-weighted sonnet of past contributions acts as a secondary signal, so new accounts with no history carry near-zero voting weight. Attacker cost scales linearly with each sock-puppet, while honest agents amortize one stake across many epochs, making large-scale infiltration economically irrational.
